subject: GammaHealth: IAM questionnaire + follow-up on SSO/SCIM/RBAC
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@gammahealth.com>, procurement@gammahealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood IAM questionnaire and a couple clarifications

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. We attached our standard IAM questionnaire (we'll send via secure link), but I had a few quick clarifications before we populate the spreadsheet:

1) SSO: Do you support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows? We need IdP-initiated for our Okta flows and SP-initiated for some legacy apps.
2) OIDC: Any support for OIDC connections (authorization code + PKCE) and token introspection endpoints? We have hybrid clients.
3) SCIM: Is SCIM v2 supported for provisioning? Can you handle group sync and delta (incremental) sync? Also curious about rate limits on SCIM endpoints.
4) RBAC & delegated admin: Can we create org-scoped roles and delegate admin for sub-teams?
5) Audit logs & retention: We need 2 years of admin/audit logs available.

If you can provide concise answers and point us to the capability matrix + any sample metadata endpoints, we'll drop the spreadsheet back to you for completion and legal can start procurement.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Security Architect, GammaHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@gammahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood IAM questionnaire and a couple clarifications

Hi Olivia — great to hear from you. We answered each item below and attached a compact capability matrix plus a filled example of the spreadsheet where helpful. Short answers first, details after:

1) SSO: Yes — we support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML 2.0. We publish a metadata URL for SP-initiated flows and can provide per-tenant ACS and entityID. SAML assertions support signed and encrypted assertions; NameID formats: emailAddress, persistent, transient.
2) OIDC: Supported — Authorization Code with PKCE is supported for browser/native flows. We expose a token introspection endpoint and support standard claims (email, sub, roles) and custom claim mappings.
3) SCIM: SCIM 2.0 supported for user provisioning and groups. We support bulk import, incremental delta sync via 'startIndex/totalResults' and 'If-Modified-Since' style polling, and can map external group IDs to Redwood roles. Default SCIM rate limit: 60 req/min per tenant, configurable with dedicated capacity.
4) RBAC & delegated admin: Yes — RBAC is hierarchical (org -> workspace -> model-route). You can create custom roles and assign scope-limited admin privileges (billing-only, security-admin, ops-admin). Delegated admin accounts can be restricted to specific workspace IDs.
5) Audit logs: Admin and auth events retained for 24 months by default for enterprise plans; longer retention available as an add-on. Logs are exportable via API and delivered to S3/GCS destinations or pushed to SIEM via webhook.

Details and notes:
- SAML metadata: https://auth.redwood.com/metadata/sp/<tenant-id> (we'll provide a per-tenant URL in the onboarding doc).
- Assertion attributes: we include 'email', 'name', 'roles' and can add custom attributes.
- OIDC scopes: openid, profile, email, roles; support for client credentials for machine-to-machine flows.
- SCIM group handling: group membership changes can be pushed (PATCH) and we support a 'membership' attribute that maps to RBAC roles.
- SCIM pagination: support for 'startIndex' and 'itemsPerPage' and delta sync via 'schemas: urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse' metadata.
- Rate limiting: as above; for Dedicated customers we can raise limits and provide a private endpoint.
- Service accounts & API keys: scoped API keys exist; service accounts can be limited to read-only or write scopes and tied to a workspace.
- MFA: We enforce MFA for admin console via TOTP, SSO enforcement available for all users. Support for FIDO2/U2F coming as opt-in this quarter.

I've attached 'redwood-iam-capability-matrix-20260329.pdf' with short evidence points (config screenshots, sample audit log entries) and 'gammahealth-questions-filled.xlsx' as a completed baseline. Let us know any follow-ups and we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with our product security engineer.

Thanks,

Marissa, thanks for the quick turnaround — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our engineering team after we reviewed the matrix:

A) SCIM conflict resolution: If an incoming SCIM PATCH tries to change a user's email (primary identifier), how does Redwood handle conflicts vs local edits? Do you support attribute precedence (source of truth) and are there hooks to reject changes?

B) OIDC token lifetime: What are the default access and refresh token TTLs? Can they be tuned per-tenant?

C) Audit export frequency: For SIEM ingestion we'd like near-real-time exports (push). Do you have webhooks or streaming export capability for admin/auth events?

Also procurement asked whether we can get a signed BAA and a 2-year log retention commitment as part of the commercial SOW. Procurement copied.

--Daniel
Lead Engineer, Integrations, GammaHealth

Subject: Re: Redwood IAM questionnaire and a couple clarifications

Hi Daniel — answers below, and I've looped in Monica (CS) and Laura (Security & Contracts) so we can follow up on the BAA/SOW items.

A) SCIM conflict resolution: By default, SCIM is treated as authoritative for attributes marked by the customer as the source of truth during onboarding. We support attribute precedence rules: you can mark attributes as 'idp-preferred' or 'redwood-preferred' via the tenant config. If a conflict occurs on a primary identifier (email), the system rejects the SCIM change and emits a 'conflict' event to the audit stream; you can configure to auto-accept or require manual reconciliation. We also provide webhooks for 'scim.conflict' so your provisioning system can reconcile automatically.

B) OIDC token lifetime: Defaults: access token = 1 hour, refresh token = 30 days (rotating refresh tokens). Yes — lifetimes are configurable at the tenant level and can be overridden per OAuth client. We also support short-lived access tokens with session cookies for browser sessions.

C) Audit export: We support push-based webhooks for admin/auth events (near-real-time) and streaming exports to a secure S3/GCS bucket. Webhooks deliver JSON payloads and can be configured to batch at 1s/30s/5m intervals depending on throughput. For Dedicated/Private customers we also offer Kafka connectors.

On procurement items: Laura will send a standard BAA and proposed language for a 24-month log-retention clause; we can include this in the SOW and also offer an add-on for immutable archival to a customer-owned bucket.

Next steps:
- Laura to circulate a redline-ready BAA by Tue 2026-03-31.
- Monica to schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough to demo SCIM conflict handling and audit webhook delivery the week of Apr 5.
- We'll update the SCIM rate-limit terms in the SOW for Dedicated customers.

If that works, we'll await your confirmation and then route to legal/procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
